findings.issue_text: [High/bug] AssignmentSource.to_dict() (via asdict) emits `queued` as a raw datetime object, and this dict is passed directly as a Celery kwarg in sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(...); datetime is not JSON-serializable, so with Sentry's JSON task serializer this raises an EncodeError at enqueue time inside GroupAssignee.assign/deassign, breaking every inbound→outbound assignee sync whenever a source is set. Tests don't catch it because self.tasks() executes tasks inline without serialization.

[Medium/data] `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` in AssignmentSource is a class-level default evaluated once at module import, so every instance shares the same import-time timestamp; use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

[Medium/api] The `assignment_source` parameter was added to the wrong abstract method: it's on `sync_status_outbound`, but the task (sync_assignee_outbound.py:60) passes it to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(...)`, whose abstract signature was not updated; the parameter only reaches implementations via **kwargs, the ABC contract is wrong, and sync_status_outbound now advertises a parameter nothing passes or uses.

[Medium/concurrency] The cycle guard only blocks the identical integration_id; with two different integrations (e.g., Jira and GitHub) linked to the same group with inbound+outbound assignee sync enabled, assignments still ping-pong indefinitely (Jira→Sentry→GitHub→Sentry→Jira…) because each hop has a different source, so the PR's stated goal of preventing sync cycles is only partially met.

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py has no test for the positive path the code comment promises: an assignment_source from integration A with a linked external issue on integration B must still sync outbound; only the source=None and same-integration-blocked cases are covered, so a regression that over-blocks (e.g., comparing provider or org instead of integration id) would go undetected.

[Low/bug] from_dict in src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:29-35 swallows all ValueError/TypeError and silently returns None with no logging, so a malformed assignment_source_dict silently disables the anti-cycle guard (degrading into the loop condition this PR aims to prevent); it also performs no type validation — after a JSON round-trip `queued` would be accepted as a str, violating the dataclass type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] The `assignment_source` parameter was added to the wrong abstract method: it's on `sync_status_outbound`, but the task (sync_assignee_outbound.py:60) passes it to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(...)`, whose abstract signature was not updated; the parameter only reaches implementations via **kwargs, the ABC contract is wrong, and sync_status_outbound now advertises a parameter nothing passes or uses.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new `assignment_source` value is propagated through `GroupAssignee`/`sync_group_assignee_outbound` into the Celery task and then passed as a keyword to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` (tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py). However, the only abstract outbound method signature that was updated in the mixin is `sync_status_outbound(..., assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None, **kwargs)` (integrations/mixins/issues.py), not `sync_assignee_outbound`. That creates an API/ABC inconsistency (and `sync_status_outbound` now advertises a parameter that is not shown being passed anywhere in this diff). Whether this is a runtime-breaking bug depends on existing `sync_assignee_outbound` signatures outside the diff (e.g., if they already accept `**kwargs`), which cannot be verified from the provided patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] The cycle guard only blocks the identical integration_id; with two different integrations (e.g., Jira and GitHub) linked to the same group with inbound+outbound assignee sync enabled, assignments still ping-pong indefinitely (Jira→Sentry→GitHub→Sentry→Jira…) because each hop has a different source, so the PR's stated goal of preventing sync cycles is only partially met.

adjudication.rationale: The new cycle guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only short-circuits when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (i.e., it blocks re-propagation back to the same integration), while explicitly allowing “other integrations to propagate changes outward” (comment + logic). From the diff, inbound assignment sets `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` in `sync_group_assignee_inbound`, and outbound propagation forwards that source through the Celery task into `should_sync`. This means assignments originating from Integration A will still be synced outbound to Integration B, and if B then triggers an inbound assignment back into Sentry, the source becomes B and Sentry will sync back out to A. The diff doesn’t prove external webhooks will create that loop, but it does show the guard is not designed to prevent multi-integration ping-pong cycles, so the finding is a valid scope/edge-case concern rather than a directly verifiable defect.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds new cycle-prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` that returns False only when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (issues.py). The updated tests in `tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py` cover (1) `assignment_source=None` still syncing outbound, and (2) matching-source-integration blocking outbound. There is no test asserting the intended positive path where `assignment_source` is present but refers to a *different* integration than the linked external issue’s integration, which should still allow syncing. That’s a specific gap around the newly introduced conditional and could miss regressions that over-block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] from_dict in src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:29-35 swallows all ValueError/TypeError and silently returns None with no logging, so a malformed assignment_source_dict silently disables the anti-cycle guard (degrading into the loop condition this PR aims to prevent); it also performs no type validation — after a JSON round-trip `queued` would be accepted as a str, violating the dataclass type.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None` without logging (new file `assignment_source.py`, `from_dict`). In `sync_assignee_outbound`, a `None` parsed source is then passed to `installation.should_sync(...)`, and the anti-cycle check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only runs when `sync_source` is not `None`. So malformed `assignment_source_dict` would indeed bypass the anti-cycle guard. However, in the paths added by this PR, `assignment_source_dict` is produced via `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` (and tests cover that), so under normal operation it should be well-formed; the lack of logging/runtime type validation (e.g., `queued` potentially being a string after JSON) is a robustness/observability concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect in the shown flow.
